title: Revit governed worksharing session, maintenance, upgrade and recovery
test_intent: Determine whether a workshared Revit model follows the approved multi-user authoring path and whether maintenance, version upgrades, and recovery actions are governed and traceable rather than ad-hoc.

applicability.applies_when: A Revit model is workshared or a governed maintenance, upgrade, or recovery action is being reviewed.
applicability.not_applicable_when: The tested model is not workshared and no maintenance, upgrade, or recovery event is within scope.

required_evidence: authoritative model/source location or cloud collaboration context
synchronization or publish history where available
maintenance, upgrade, or recovery records when such events occurred
approved role/RACI or escalation path where required

result_logic.pass: The applicable worksharing path is followed, synchronization/publication behavior is consistent with the project rule, ownership remains bounded, and any maintenance, upgrade, or recovery action is traceable to the approved configuration and evidence requirements.
result_logic.fail: A positive violation is found against an available governed rule, including bypassing the approved authoring path, propagating an unstable session, performing an upgrade without a recoverable pre-upgrade state, or resuming production without required post-upgrade validation.
result_logic.not_applicable: No governed worksharing, maintenance, upgrade, or recovery rule applies to the tested scope.
result_logic.indeterminate: The project worksharing configuration, maintenance cadence, upgrade authority, or recovery basis required for evaluation is unavailable or incomplete.

provenance.migration_note: Appendix E ATS covering the broader worksharing/session-health behavior not covered by ATS-REVIT-WORKSET-001. Project-specific cadence and deployment mechanics remain inputs rather than enterprise defaults.
